title: Greenfield SDK seedling: compact starter templates for Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP & CLI (streaming + retries)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Deliver a compact, opinionated starter pack that demonstrates best-practice SDK usage across Next.js (TS), FastAPI (Python), Go HTTP servers, and a small CLI. Focus areas: streaming ergonomics, explicit retry configuration, token/batching trade-offs, and small cookbook snippets that teams can copy into production. This is intentionally small and prescriptive — the goal is low cognitive load for engineers onboarding Redwood SDKs to production workloads.

Scope and deliverables:
- Four minimal apps (Next.js web app example, FastAPI backend example, Go HTTP server example, CLI example) each with a focused README and a single page/demo endpoint.
- Cookbook snippets showing: streaming responses (client and server patterns), structured retries with jittered exponential backoff, idempotency strategies, and safe request cancellation.
- SDK surface notes: expose a RetryPolicy config (max_attempts, initial_backoff_ms, max_backoff_ms, jitter_strategy, retry_on_status, idempotency_key_hint). Examples show recommended defaults for latency-sensitive (interactive) vs cost-sensitive (batch) workloads.
- Streaming ergonomics guidance: prefer async iterators / ReadableStream / channels instead of raw byte buffers; include resumption token pattern for long-running streams; demonstrate graceful reconnect and partial-output merging.
- CI example: simple GitHub Actions workflow to run unit tests + integration tests against the local sandbox / smoke tests that assert streaming shape, backoff behavior, and idempotency semantics.
- Telemetry suggestions: add SDK counters and histograms for streaming_error_rate, retry_count, avg_stream_latency, max_resume_attempts; tie to Console dashboards.

Non-goals:
- This ticket is not an exhaustive SDK refactor. We will not change core runtime behavior, nor add new server-side resume tokens without a follow-up runtime change. If runtime work is required, we will file a dedicated infra ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Minimal Next.js example that streams tokens to the browser using the JS SDK ReadableStream pattern and includes a short README with run steps
FastAPI example demonstrating async iterator consumption of server stream and safe cancellation handling
Go HTTP server example exposing a streaming endpoint and a small client showing chunk framing and reconnect logic
CLI example that supports both sync (complete response) and streaming modes with progress and a --retries option
Cookbook snippets for retries, idempotency_key usage, and recommended RetryPolicy defaults included in SDK docs
Automated smoke test(s) that assert retry logic (simulate transient 5xx) and streaming resumption behavior
Links to a consolidated GitHub repo and a design doc (Drive) included in the ticket
Telemetry events emitted by SDK examples and verified in a local dev dashboard (can be a mocked sink)
tasks: Write Next.js example and README (TSX, 2 pages: demo + README)
Write FastAPI example and README (async streaming consumer)
Write Go HTTP server example and client sample
Write CLI example (Go or Python) that demonstrates both sync and streaming modes
Author cookbook snippets and place them under /cookbook in the repo
Create GitHub Actions workflow for CI smoke tests
Add minimal telemetry hooks and a local mocked sink for verification
Peer review of examples and README by DX/Docs and one SDK maintainer
Create final PR linking examples to central SDK docs
